headline: Executive order directs federal agencies to plan for climate risks in the international development work they fund.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order tells federal agencies that run international development programs to consider climate-related risks, such as extreme weather, when planning and funding projects abroad. The aim is for those projects to hold up better against climate effects. No summary was provided, so specific requirements and deadlines are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that run international development programs
who_it_affects.how: They would need to factor climate risks into how they plan and fund projects in other countries.

who_it_affects.group: Communities in other countries that receive US development aid
who_it_affects.how: Projects serving them may be designed with climate risks in mind.

who_it_affects.group: Organizations and contractors that carry out US-funded development projects
who_it_affects.how: They may face new planning considerations related to climate risks.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed September 23, 2014; executive orders usually take effect when signed.
